__doc: THE MODIFIER KEY REGISTRY. Every probability, penalty and cost the match engine works out passes through one function - resolve(key, base, context) in src/engine/modifiers.ts - and this file is the list of keys it accepts. Badges and playstyles are nothing more than modifiers registered against a key here. If a key does not exist, any badge hooking into it is dead code, which is exactly what this file exists to prevent.
__how_it_works: The engine computes a BASE value out of the player's sub-stats, exactly as it always did, then hands it to resolve(). With nothing registered, resolve() hands it straight back - that is why build step 3 changes no numbers at all. Once badges and playstyles arrive they register against a key, declare which situations they care about, and reshape the value on its way through.
__no_stacking: Modifiers on the same key DO NOT STACK. If three of them apply at once, the strongest single one wins and the other two do nothing. That is deliberate: it stops a player stacking six badges onto one number and breaking the game, and it means every badge is worth having on its own rather than only in combination.
__clamping: Each key declares a `clamp` shape. `probability` is held inside 0.01-0.99, so nothing is ever certain or impossible. `substat` never exceeds 99. `amount` never goes below zero. `signed` is left alone, for the one value that is meaningfully negative: LAN_PENALTY is a swing, minus for a player who shrinks on stage and plus for one who grows, so clamping it at zero would delete stage fright entirely. IMPORTANT: the clamp is applied ONLY when a modifier actually changed the value. An untouched base value passes through exactly as the engine computed it, which is what keeps build step 3 a true no-op refactor.
__wired_in: `wiredIn` says which build step actually calls resolve() for this key. `3` means it is live now. A later number means the key is DECLARED and resolvable, but the engine has no such concept yet - the phases gain it at that step. `npm run verify:modifiers` prints the ledger and fails if a key claiming to be live is never called during a real session, so a key cannot quietly rot.

keys.base: The chance of winning a fight the duo chose to take. Comes from the mid-game weight set in balance.json - flicks and tracking lead it - run through the Fighting multiplier.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - the optional mid-game fight, the drop fight, and the fight a blown rotate forces on you.

keys.base: The chance of winning the contested drop - the race for the first gun. Driven by the offspawn weight set, fifty_fifties above all.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - PHASE 1, when the drop is contested.

keys.base: The chance of getting into the next zone in a position worth having. Positioning and rotation.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - the first rotate, and the unavoidable pressure check in every mid-game zone.

keys.base: Mats burned. Build Efficiency already cuts the endgame per-circle cost; every other spend is a flat number out of balance.json.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - every call to spendMats, plus the mats a reboot costs.

keys.base: Damage taken getting into the circle when the rotate goes wrong. Rotation quality against the zone timer.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - the shield lost on a failed rotate and on losing ground in a zone.

keys.base: Damage taken breaking off a fight rather than committing to it. Reset Timing and Movement.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - the shield lost when a lost fight ends in a disengage instead of a death.

keys.base: The opponent's chance of turning your disengage into a dead duo instead of a knocked player. Cut by the duo's Reset Timing and Movement.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - takeCasualty, the wipe chance on a lost fight.

keys.base: Power lost while a man down. Scales with how outnumbered you are - a 1v2 costs less than a 1v3.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - situationalMod, whenever one player is on the floor.

keys.base: The chance a bad rotate turns into a fight you did not choose. Rises with how long you are exposed and how poor your positioning is.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - the death chance on a failed rotate.

keys.base: The chance of getting a downed partner back into the game. Communication and Movement.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - tryReboot.
keys.__note: In this engine saving a partner IS the reboot: you break off, survive, and rebuild them. If a later step adds a separate mid-fight save, it hooks the same key.

keys.base: The Big Stage Nerve swing, read ONLY at events flagged lan:true. Negative for a player who shrinks on stage, positive for one who grows.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - buildStates, once per player per match.
keys.__note: Build step 5 turns this from a flat points shift into the multiplier the brief asks for. The key does not change, only what feeds it.

keys.base: How wide this player's random roll is. Consistency, inverted - a consistent player has a narrow spread.
keys.calledFrom: sim.ts - buildStates, the per-match form roll.

keys.base: Accuracy lost while firing and being fired at. Flat penalty, cut by composure.
keys.calledFrom: NOT YET. The engine resolves a fight in one exchange - there is no notion of shooting while being shot at until the phases are rewritten.

keys.base: Power lost at range. Rises with engagement distance.
keys.calledFrom: NOT YET. Fights have no range yet.

keys.base: The chance of missing the edit you meant. Edit Accuracy, made worse by pressure.
keys.calledFrom: NOT YET. Edits are folded into the fight roll rather than being their own moment.

keys.base: Power lost by whichever side does not hold the piece.
keys.calledFrom: NOT YET. Piece advantage is per-player match state, which arrives at step 4.

keys.base: The chance of taking the opponent's piece. Piece Control and Edit IQ.
keys.calledFrom: NOT YET.

keys.base: Damage taken when a piece steal fails.
keys.calledFrom: NOT YET.

keys.base: Power lost while below the opponent.
keys.calledFrom: NOT YET. has_height is per-player match state, which arrives at step 4.

keys.base: Power lost dropping into more players than you brought. Scales with how many are contesting.
keys.calledFrom: NOT YET. A contested drop is currently a coin-weighted fight with no count of who else landed.

keys.base: Power lost fighting on worse loot. Scales with loot tier - grey through gold.
keys.calledFrom: NOT YET. loot_tier is per-player match state, which arrives at step 4.

keys.base: Which partner's Decision Making the duo actually rotates on. Currently the engine blends both.
keys.calledFrom: NOT YET. Needs a caller to be a real, named thing rather than an average.

keys.base: Damage taken while saving a partner.
keys.calledFrom: NOT YET. A reboot currently costs mats and nothing else.
